title: Use proportional symbols when counts run too far apart for a bar.
rule: Draw one circle for each count, its area in proportion to the count on one scale for every circle, the radius by the square root (Rule 14.4). Name each circle and print its count beside it, or inside the circle the title names, which takes the subject ink; the rest take the track gray with a thin edge. Add a key of nested circles at round counts that reaches past the largest. A count whose circle would draw under a few pixels prints in words beside the circles, with the reason.
use_when: The reader asks how many there are of each kind, and the counts span so wide a range that a bar for the smallest would vanish, such as the 39,555 special districts and 3,031 county governments the Census Bureau counted in 2022.

use_instead.when: The counts sit close enough to rank by length
The counts are parts of one whole the reader sees at once
Each count belongs to a place on a map

text: Area grows with the count while the radius grows with its square root, so a count 13 times another draws a circle about 3.6 times as wide, and the smallest still shows. Areas are harder to compare exactly than lengths, so every circle prints its count and the key gives the scale.
why.basis: Design judgment, from the chart system our founder and editor approved in November 2026

builders: Form proportional-symbols: node work/build/chart-kit/oa-chart.mjs build s86; labels.named sets the circle the title names, labels.words_only the rows printed in words with labels.word and labels.words, and labels.key_steps the key’s counts.
